claims.claim: The optimized algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M), where M=Σ_t d(p_t), d counts descents, and p_{t+1}=reverse(D(p_t)) followed by U(p_t).
claims.evidence: The transition formula is correct for ordinary mark-all-then-MoveToFront sorting, but not for the source’s literal optimized FIFO pseudocode. That pseudocode PushBacks newly discovered marks and later PopFronts them, so their order can differ from left-to-right shelf order. On the witness, T uses the second-round order (2,1) and sorts, while the optimized queue contains (1,2) and leaves (2,1,3,4,5,6). Thus the claimed orbit, and hence M as defined from that orbit, is not the optimized algorithm’s orbit. The ordinary T orbit takes 5 moves in 2 rounds; the literal optimized algorithm takes 6 moves in 3 rounds.
claims.witness: p=(4,1,5,2,6,3): after round 1 the state is (3,2,1,4,5,6), but the optimized next queue is (1,2); its round-2 state is (2,1,3,4,5,6), whereas T gives (1,2,3,4,5,6).
claims.search_method: Implemented independent exact versions of T, ordinary mark-then-MoveToFront, the source-literal optimized queue algorithm, and an array-backed linked-list version; cross-checked them and exhaustively tested every permutation through n=9.

claims.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
claims.evidence: Let i be the largest unfixed value. All larger values form a permanent fixed suffix, so i lies strictly before position i and cannot be a descent bottom. In a round, moving a descent bottom left of i causes one left shift when removed and one right shift when prepended, for net zero; moving one right of i shifts i right exactly once. Hence its position increases by q_t. When the phase ends at position i, Σq_t=i−s_i. Since every moved element lies either left or right of i, the phase move cost is exactly (i−s_i)+Σℓ_t. This argument is independent of the order in which the marked set is processed. The checker additionally verified the identities on every orbit through n=9 under both T and the source-literal optimized process.
claims.search_method: Completed a direct position-invariant proof and exhaustively checked active-value position increments, phase sums, marked sets, and costs for all permutations of sizes at most 9 under both transition models.

claims.claim: The worst-case lower bound improves rigorously to Ω(n^{3/2}); indeed one explicit family incurs (4√2/3+o(1))n^{3/2} moves before its largest element is fixed.
claims.evidence: The staircase calculation concerns the ordinary transition T, not the source’s optimized FIFO process. The claimed family reduction already fails at its third boundary: for P_6, T gives prefix F_3=(3,1,2), but the optimized algorithm gives (1,3,2). Therefore the asserted state identity F_m,n,m+1,… and the summation derived from it do not prove a lower bound or the stated coefficient for the requested optimized algorithm. Exact checks found the staircase descent formula valid for the abstract T system through m=10000, reinforcing that the flaw is the invalid transfer between algorithms, not a finite failure of that auxiliary recurrence.
claims.witness: P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5): after three rounds T is (3,1,2,6,4,5), while the source-literal optimized algorithm is (1,3,2,6,4,5).
claims.search_method: Compared the claimed P_n/T prefix recurrence round-by-round against a literal execution of the optimized PushBack/PopFront pseudocode, and separately checked the abstract T staircase with exact integers.

claims.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves are 0,1,3,7,13,21,33,47,63.
claims.evidence: Complete enumeration shows that this sequence is exactly the maximum for ordinary T, but not for the source-literal optimized algorithm. Its exact maxima for n=1,…,9 are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53. The discrepancy begins at n=4, where the claimed maximum is 7 but exhaustive optimized execution gives 6.
claims.witness: n=4: all 24 permutations were enumerated; the source-literal optimized maximum is 6, attained by (4,1,2,3), rather than the claimed 7.
claims.search_method: Enumerated every permutation for n≤9 and iterated each to termination using two cross-checked exact implementations of the optimized pseudocode; separately enumerated T to identify the source of the claimed sequence.

claims.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
claims.evidence: For the source-literal optimized process, the even-then-odd permutation of size 4096 makes exactly 49,545,006 moves, exceeding 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120. Thus no charging proof assigning at most two moves to every unordered pair can bound all executions. The draft’s quoted 50,546,772 count and its P_13 count of 161 belong to T; literal optimized P_13 makes 97 moves. Those numerical mismatches do not invalidate the weaker listed claim because the corrected size-4096 count remains a decisive counterexample.
claims.witness: p=(2,4,…,4096,1,3,…,4095): the source-literal optimized algorithm makes 49,545,006 moves, while 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120.
claims.search_method: Ran an exact array-backed doubly-linked-list simulation, cross-validated against a vector implementation on every permutation through n=9, and compared the integer move total with the exact pair threshold.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an asymptotically tight worst-case complexity. Even on its own terms, the draft leaves an unmatched Ω(n^{3/2})–O(n^3) interval and therefore could only be partial. More importantly, its headline claim that this interval is certified is not established for the requested optimized algorithm: the draft analyzes the ordinary transition T, while the source’s PushBack/PopFront optimized pseudocode follows different states and has different finite maxima. The phase decomposition and the failure of a twice-per-pair charging approach survive as valid structural progress, but neither supplies an improved asymptotic bound. Consequently the final writeup overclaims target coverage, and claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is overstated because its advertised partial resolution is the invalid Ω(n^{3/2}) transfer.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and baseline draft; used no web, retrieval database, prior run, receipt, or verification report.
Derived the ordinary mark-all-then-MoveToFront transition symbolically and compared it with the source-literal optimized queue semantics.
Implemented independent exact T, ordinary-move, optimized-vector, and optimized-linked-list simulators without floating-point decisions.
Exhaustively enumerated all 409,113 permutations of sizes at most 9 under both T and the literal optimized algorithm.
Verified the phase-position and phase-cost identities on all enumerated orbits under both models.
Checked the abstract staircase descent formula through m=10000 and the P_n/T prefix identity through n=300.
Reproduced T’s P_13 and size-4096 counts, then recomputed both witnesses under the literal optimized algorithm.
Confirmed the corrected size-4096 optimized witness exceeds the exact twice-per-pair threshold.
